subtitulo: Earth has a fever. Bring it down with solutions that already exist.
semilla_ayuda: The name decides how your planet starts. The same name gives the same world.
toca_celda: Tap a tile on the planet to see what can be done there.
nada_aqui: Nothing can be built on this tile yet.
politicas_ayuda: Big policies are paid with Hope.
potencial: Project Drawdown: {a} to {b} Gt a year
err_bioma: That solution doesn't fit this biome.
revelada: Exposed: {nombre}. Its real effect was far smaller, and it costs the planet Life.
inf_permafrost: Tipping point: permafrost has started thawing. It releases emissions you can't switch off.
inf_corales: Tipping point: tropical coral reefs are bleaching. Life drops.
inf_amazonia: Tipping point: the Amazon is turning into savanna. More emissions.
choque: Termination shock: removing the aerosols brought the hidden heat back at once.
dato: In the real world · {nombre}: according to Project Drawdown, it could avoid or remove {a} to {b} GtCO₂e a year.
dato_sin: In the real world · {nombre}: Project Drawdown hasn't published how much it can avoid yet.
fin_victoria_txt: Temperature peaked and fell ten years in a row, with net-negative emissions.
fin_derrota_vida_txt: Biodiversity collapsed and ecosystems stopped removing carbon.
fin_derrota_esperanza_txt: People stopped believing it could be done and the transition stalled.
fin_derrota_tiempo_txt: 2150 arrived and temperature didn't come down.
pol_cerrar_carbon_txt: −15% energy emissions. Fossil lock-in makes it pricier.
pol_fin_subsidios_txt: The fossil economy starts shrinking on its own every year.
pol_moratoria_deforestacion_txt: −40% forest emissions; Life degrades much less.
evita: Avoids up to {g} Gt a year
captura: Removes up to {g} Gt a year
g_hola: Hi! I'm Ceiba, like the sacred tree of many peoples of the Americas, the one that joins earth and sky. I'll show you the game one bit at a time. Your job is to cool the planet down with solutions that already exist.
g_temp: Earth is already 1.5 °C warmer than before the Industrial Revolution. In 2024 we crossed that line for the first time. Every extra tenth of a degree brings more fires, droughts and hurricanes.
g_emis: It warms because of the greenhouse gases (GHG) we release: CO₂, methane and nitrous oxide. They trap heat like a blanket. Today humanity releases 57 gigatonnes (Gt) a year, that is, 57 billion tonnes. As long as that number is above zero, the planet keeps warming.
g_meta: This is your world's history. The orange line is temperature and the teal one, emissions. You win when temperature falls 10 years in a row and your emissions are below zero, meaning you remove more carbon than you release.
g_barras: Cutting GHG isn't enough. Also look after Life (forests, reefs, animals) and Hope (the people pushing for change). If either hits zero, you lose. If the planet passes 3 °C, you lose too.
g_tocar: Let's start with a city. The blinking tiles are cities. Tap one: I've turned Bogotá towards you.
g_cajon: Each card is a real solution, measured by Project Drawdown, a group of scientists who calculated how much each one can cut the world's emissions. The green number is the most it would avoid if the whole planet adopted it. Tap a card's i and I'll tell you more. Pick one and build it.
g_recursos: Building costs energy and materials. They refill every year, but they have a cap and what you don't spend is lost. Every terrain produces something: forests and crops give materials; deserts, grasslands and sea give energy. If you have too much of one, swap it with the arrows button.
g_siguiente: Each turn is a year. When you can't afford anything else, end the year.
g_despues: This card tells you how emissions and temperature changed, and what happened around the world.
g_mejorar: Solutions start slow and speed up as your world adopts them. Tap one of your buildings to upgrade it, up to level 5. New solutions unlock every year, similar to the ones you develop most. Before building, read the i: not all of them deliver what they promise.
g_a_trampa: That solution didn't work as promised. Project Drawdown doesn't recommend it: its real effect was tiny and it harms Life. People felt fooled and Hope dropped. If you want, demolish it by tapping the building with the red sign.
g_a_evento: A disaster knocked down some buildings. More heat brings more events. Life softens them, and mangroves and salt marshes protect coasts.
g_a_inflexion: You crossed a tipping point, a change on Earth that doesn't come back, like thawing permafrost. It releases emissions you can't switch off.
g_a_esperanza: Hope is falling. It rises when people see results (emissions or temperature going down) and with people-centred solutions like public transit, bikes, food and compost. It drops with disasters, exposed traps and investing in only a few regions. Big policies are paid with Hope.
g_a_vida: Life is in danger. It rises if you protect and restore ecosystems: forests, peatlands, mangroves, seagrass. Heat, background deforestation and traps drain it.
g_a_negativas: Your emissions are below zero: your world now removes more than it releases. The real world removes about 2.2 Gt a year, and 99.9% of it is done by forests (The State of CDR, 2026).
g_a_racha: Temperature has been falling for a few years. Keep it up for 10 in a row and you reverse climate change.
g_a_recursos: You have a lot of energy and the cap will waste it. Spend it or swap it for materials with the arrows button.
tip_temp: Temperature: how much warmer your planet is than before industry (1850-1900). El Niño raises it a few tenths some years and La Niña lowers it. At 3 °C you lose.
tip_emis: Net emissions: the greenhouse gases your world releases in a year, minus what it removes, in gigatonnes (billions of tonnes) of CO₂ equivalent. Get them below zero.
tip_ener: Energy: refills every year. Solar, wind, efficiency (every LED frees energy) and desert, grassland and sea terrain give it. It has a cap.
tip_mat: Materials: refill every year. Recycling, compost and forest, crop and mountain terrain give them. They have a cap.
tip_vida: Life: biodiversity. It rises by protecting and restoring ecosystems; it falls with heat, deforestation and traps. More Life means nature removes more CO₂ and disasters hit softer. At 0 you lose.
tip_esp: Hope: the people pushing for change. It rises when they see results and with people-centred solutions; it falls with disasters, injustice and exposed traps. High Hope makes everything cheaper and pays for policies. At 0 you lose.
gl_drawdown_txt: A nonprofit that reviewed hundreds of climate solutions and calculated how much each one can reduce emissions. The game's 166 solutions come from its Drawdown Explorer (2025). Some are rated not recommended: in the game they're traps.
gl_gt_txt: Gigatonnes of CO₂ equivalent per year. A gigatonne is a billion tonnes. "Equivalent" because methane and other gases are counted as the CO₂ that would warm the same. Today the world emits about 57 Gt a year (UNEP, 2024).
gl_temp_txt: Warming above pre-industrial times. It follows all the CO₂ ever accumulated: while we emit, it rises; if we emit below zero, it falls slowly. Methane warms hard but doesn't last, so cutting it cools fast.
gl_netas_txt: When you remove more CO₂ than you release: restoring forests, peatlands, mangroves, or with technology. It's the only way temperature goes down.
gl_adopcion_txt: How much of a solution's potential the world already uses. It grows in an S-curve: slow, then fast, then full. Upgrading a solution pushes it.
gl_trampas_txt: Solutions Project Drawdown doesn't recommend: carbon capture on coal plants, corn ethanol, ocean fertilization... They look cheap and fast. Later it turns out their effect was tiny and they harm Life.
gl_politicas_txt: Big decisions, like closing coal plants, paid with Hope. They cut a whole sector's emissions at once.
gl_inflexion_txt: Parts of Earth that change for good past a certain heat: permafrost, corals, the Amazon (Armstrong McKay et al., 2022).
tabla_compartida: Scores of everyone playing at this link.
tabla_link: Play the shared version to compete with others: {link}
pts_peor: Your best score is higher, so that one stays.
pts_sin_permiso: You can see the table, but to appear on it you need contributor access. Ask whoever shared the link.
construir_en: Tap a card to build it here
comerciar_txt: Give {n} of one resource and get 1 of the other.
err_tope: That resource is already at its cap.
info_hoy: Today it avoids {g} Gt a year in the real world.
info_alcanzable: It could avoid between {a} and {b} Gt a year.
info_pct: Today that's {p} of the world's emissions.
info_preguntas: Drawdown doesn't give it a number yet. Here's how it answered:
info_estimado: Since Drawdown doesn't publish its potential, the game uses an estimate of {g} Gt a year.
info_cdr: From The State of CDR (2026): this method removes {mt} million tonnes a year worldwide today.
info_sin_ficha: It's a {cat} solution. Its number comes from Project Drawdown.
produccion: Your buildings produced {e} energy and {m} materials.
ceiba_bien: Emissions fell this year. We're on the right track.
ceiba_sube: Emissions are still rising. Solutions take time to kick in: upgrade them and build more.
ceiba_trampa: Before building, read each card's i. That's where the science is.
ceiba_vida: Life is suffering. Protect a forest or restore a mangrove.
ceiba_esp: People are getting tired. Transit and food solutions lift their spirits.
ceiba_negativas: You now remove more than you release. Now it has to hold for 10 years.
inactivo_construir: You can afford to build something. A good solution fits on the blinking tile.
inactivo_mejorar: You can upgrade one of your buildings. Tap it.
inactivo_pasar: You can't afford anything else. End the year and your resources refill.
inactivo_cambiar: You have too much of one resource and too little of the other. Swap them with the arrows button.
c_bosque: Forests and jungles: protect and restore them. They give materials.
c_cultivo: Crops and grasslands: food, biochar, silvopasture.
c_desierto: Deserts: solar farms. They give lots of energy.
c_mar: Coastal sea and ocean: seaweed, seagrass, offshore wind.
c_costa: Coasts: mangroves and salt marshes, which protect against hurricanes.
c_seco: If a tile looks brown, it's degraded or drying out from the heat.
h_meta_txt: You win when the underlying temperature falls 10 years in a row with net emissions below zero. You lose if Life or Hope hit 0, or if you pass 3 °C.
h_turno_txt: Tap a tile, build a solution, upgrade it and end the year. At the end of the year you see what happened. New solutions unlock every year.
h_recursos_txt: They refill every year with a base amount plus what your buildings and their terrain produce. They have a cap, so spend them. If you have too much of one, swap it: 3 for 1.
h_vida_txt: Rises with nature solutions (protect and restore). Falls with heat, deforestation and traps. More Life means nature removes more CO₂ and disasters hit softer.
h_esp_txt: Rises when emissions or temperature fall and with people-centred solutions (transit, food, compost). Falls with disasters, unfair investment and exposed traps. It makes everything cheaper and pays for policies.
h_trampas_txt: Some solutions promise a lot and cost little. Each card's i shows what the science says.
h_politicas_txt: Big decisions, like closing coal plants, paid with Hope. They cut a whole sector's emissions at once.
h_gt_txt: Greenhouse gases (GHG) trap heat. They're measured in gigatonnes (Gt) of CO₂ equivalent: a billion tonnes. Today the world releases 57 a year (UNEP, 2024).
h_drawdown_txt: A nonprofit that assessed hundreds of climate solutions and calculated how much each one can reduce. The game's come from its Drawdown Explorer (2025).
g_a_desbloqueo: Solutions unlock every year. Grey ones aren't ready yet, and the ones similar to what you've developed open sooner. Tap the i on a grey one to see what it is.
g_a_enso: This year had El Niño or La Niña: the Pacific Ocean warms or cools for a year or two and moves the planet's temperature a few tenths. What counts for winning is the underlying trend, not those jumps.
bloqueada_txt: Not ready yet. It opens sooner if you develop similar solutions.
enso_nino: El Niño year: the Pacific warmed and added {t} °C to the planet's temperature.
enso_nina: La Niña year: the Pacific cooled and took {t} °C off the planet's temperature.
hoy_evita: In your world it avoids {g} Gt a year today ({p}% adopted).
al_mejorar: Upgrading: adoption in your world heads to {b}% (now heading to {a}%)
info_terreno_txt: Includes what its terrain ({b}) gives, which rises at levels 3 and 5.
arbol_txt: Every year, new solutions whose requirements you already have open up. The ones in the branch you develop most come first. Tap one to see what it is.
